Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited to move to a reseller flow. We've started the onboarding questionnaire (attached) and have an immediate routing/UK-IDTA question. One of our downstream processors (EdgeTransit Ltd.) terminates TLS at a UK edge and then proxies telemetry to their US core for enrichment. The customer (a UK public sector buyer) is asking whether SCCs alone are sufficient or whether Redwood's UK Addendum / IDTA pathing is required given the termination in the UK.

Separately, procurement needs: proof that any subprocessors used by Redwood on behalf of Resaleway are covered in the DPA (we requested a subprocessor CSV but can also accept signed attestations). Can you confirm how Redwood prefers to provide subprocessor proof for reseller relationships (CSV, signed bridge letter, or per-deal attestations)?

Laura — quick legal read:

1) EdgeTransit termination in the UK (TLS termination at UK edge) is a nuance: if personal data is decrypted/processed in the UK and then transferred onward to the US, SCCs may be acceptable from an EU perspective, but UK ICO guidance leans toward an IDTA/UK Addendum if there is onward transfer outside the UK where the controller/processor model differs or where UK data subjects are involved. Given the buyer is UK public sector, we should assume they will insist on the UK Addendum unless Resaleway can demonstrate data never leaves the UK in a personal-data-decrypted form.

2) Proof of subprocessors: our standard is to provide an up-to-date subprocessor CSV (public link or per-deal snapshot). For reseller models we have three options:
   - public CSV + per-deal snapshot (fastest)
   - signed bridge letter (legal acceptance that the CSV applies to the reseller deployment)
   - per-customer attestation (when buyer demands tighter evidence)

3) Suggested ask back to Resaleway (short list):
   - Confirm EdgeTransit role and whether they decrypt/persist personal data in the UK.
   - Provide reseller commercial model (reseller as controller vs. processor) to determine whether Redwood will be a subprocessed vendor or remain a direct processor to buyer.

I've attached a short checklist we ask Legal to fill for reseller/marketplace flows. If the buyer requires UK Addendum, we'll prepare a doc and route via DocuSign; if not, we'll finalize a TIAs scope and provide CSV + signed attestation for the deal.

Attachment: uk_addendum_checklist.pdf

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Contracts
Redwood Inference

Thanks all — consolidated response and next steps: 

1) Evidence approach: for reseller flows we can provide the subprocessor CSV snapshot plus a short signed bridge letter attesting the CSV applies to the reseller deployment. That pattern has cleared procurement for multiple reseller partners; if the buyer requires additional attestation we will escalate to per-customer certification.

2) EdgeTransit: based on Resaleway's note that decryption/inspection occurs in the UK and then forwarding occurs to the US (even if pseudonymized) we should assume the buyer will request the UK Addendum. Kimberly will draft a targeted UK Addendum (narrow scope) to handle this use case and push via DocuSign.

3) Timeline:
   - Fri (EOD): Kimberly to share UK Addendum redline for Resaleway review (internal draft).
   - Mon: send DocuSign envelope for signature if Resaleway confirms.
   - Tue/Wed: finish TIA scoping (if buyer asks for TIAs we will include EdgeTransit and Redwood's dependency chain).

4) Escalation path: if buyer refuses CSV+bridge letter and demands platform-level attestation we will open an exec escalation. For now, treat CSV+bridge letter as our first-line evidence.

Related links: HubSpot deal 1245789; Laura will update deal notes when DocuSign envelope is created.

I'll attach the draft UK Addendum (narrow) once Kimberly sends it.
